text: On Sunday morning Jerry was cleaning me in the yard, when Polly stepped up to him, looking very full of something. “What is it?” said Jerry. “Well, my dear,” she said, “poor Dinah Brown has just had a letter brought to say that her mother is dangerously ill, and that she must go directly if she wishes to see her alive. The place is more than ten miles away from here, out in the country, and she says if she takes the train she should still have four miles to walk; and so weak as she is, and the baby only four weeks old, of course that would be impossible; and she wants to know if you would take her in your cab, and she promises to pay you faithfully, as she can get the money.” “Tut, tut! we'll see about that.
